one_sentence: Free will is structurally required for meaning, and the von Neumann regress terminates as a typing error via the triadic Actualizer.
executive_summary: This document argues that free will is not a philosophical preference but a structural requirement for meaning: a deterministic witness is merely a mirror, incapable of generating genuine meaning. It dissolves the von Neumann measurement regress by typing the observation chain—the Actualizer (A) is operation-level (Type₁), not object-level (Type₀), so asking 'what observes the observer?' is a type error. The unique terminating structure for actualization is exactly three roles: Generation (Type₀), Logos (Type₀), and Actualization (Type₁). Three results are declared as the Floor: the Trinity isomorphism, the structural necessity of free will (W), and God-as-axiom as the ground of the system. This establishes the boundary beneath which the system does not reason.
short_summary: This document is a formal proof that free will is structurally required for meaning and that the von Neumann regress terminates as a typing error. The core structural claim is that a genuine witness must possess an unconstrained binary choice (W) not determined by the system. Key evidence includes the exhaustive type-analysis showing exactly three roles (Generation, Logos, Actualization) with one at operation level uniquely terminates the regress. This matters because it grounds the entire Theophysics framework on a proven structural floor, linking free will, the Trinity, and God-as-axiom as the boundary of formal reasoning.
